newsitem.title: ESTONIA: SILMET TO EXPAND SHARE CAPITAL - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: SILMET TO EXPAND SHARE CAPITAL - REPORT.

text.p: The shareholders' meeting for Estonian rare earth processor Silmet voted on Monday to expand its share capital after forming itself into a group structure, the newspaper Paevaleht said on Tuesday.
Silmet will write off 7.4 million kroons of the company's existing share capital to bring its books into balance, the daily said.
The company then has the right to expand its share capital from a minimum of 40 million kroons up to 160 million kroons.
The expansion of the company's share capital will be used to finance the company's operations and is cheaper than taking a loan, Silmet board chairman Neeme Jogi was quoted as saying in Paevaleht.
The main shareholder of Silmet is Ephag As which holds 65 percent of the company.
Ephag is owned by the locally based Magnum group and private investor Thomas Waldin.
In the first half of 1997, Silmet's turnover was 95.5 million kroons and its half year loss was four million kroons.
